event.description: 48 BCE decisive battle of Caesar's Civil War

passages.gist: A general abundantly supplied by land and sea judges it safer to refuse battle and grind down his resource-starved but battle-hardened rival through famine, while elites and client rulers flock to his side.

passages.gist: A reflection on Rome's would-be conquest of distant peoples collapses into an account of civil war, climaxing as a centurion races ahead of the line to exchange vows of victory and loyalty with his general before the battle begins.

passages.gist: In the Pompeianis camp at Pharsalia, the army's renowned orator breaks his long silence to voice their vow, praying that Fortune favor their general and that his kinsman be defeated in the civil war.

passages.gist: A rhetorically charged historical narrative of the provocations, delays, and ominous portents that culminate in the decisive civil-war battle in Thessaly, where the fate of Rome and the human race is staked on a single day.

passages.gist: As a great general musters supporters against his rival on the eve of civil war, men of every rank—defector, avenging son, grieving elder, wounded veteran—rally to him, and a just senate decree wins his cause still broader sympathy.

passages.gist: After the victory at Pharsalia the victor pursues his fleeing rival toward Emathias, and though companions urge refuge in Ausonia, the defeated leader vows never to re-enter his homeland except with a disbanded army, recalling he might once have fought at home.
